name: Micaiah
bio:
Micaiah son of Imlah was the one true prophet of the LORD whom Ahab hated, "for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil," when Ahab and Jehoshaphat of Judah were deciding whether to attack Ramoth Gilead. Four hundred court prophets, including Zedekiah son of Chenaanah with his iron horns, had already promised victory. The messenger sent to fetch Micaiah urged him to agree with them, but Micaiah answered, "As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak" (1 Kings 22:1-14).

Brought before the two kings, Micaiah first answered sarcastically in the other prophets' own words — "Go, and prosper" — until Ahab pressed him to swear to tell the truth. He then told of a vision: Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd, the LORD asking who would persuade Ahab to go up and die at Ramoth Gilead, and a lying spirit volunteering to deceive him through all his prophets, sent by the LORD himself to bring about the evil already decreed against Ahab (1 Kings 22:15-23). Zedekiah struck Micaiah on the cheek for this; Micaiah told him he would see for himself the day he hid in an inner chamber. Ahab had Micaiah thrown into prison on bread and water until his safe return — a return Micaiah predicted would never come, since "the LORD hath not spoken by me" if it did (1 Kings 22:24-28). Ahab died at Ramoth Gilead exactly as Micaiah had foretold.
